comparator.name: UCU Liberal Arts and Sciences
comparator.route: Bachelor of Arts with an interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences major
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026-2027 Academic Rules and Regulations define a 180-EC, six-semester Liberal Arts and Sciences degree with at least 45 EC at level 3. All students complete Academic Core in semester 1, first-year breadth across Humanities, Science and Social Sciences, and one Language and Culture course by semester 4. For the generic target, the representative route is the formally available interdomain BA major combining Humanities and Social Sciences: it best expresses the programme's broad interdisciplinary identity without selecting for UCR fit. The BA major contains at least 75 EC, including a 15-EC final-year thesis and tracks in at least two disciplines; at least 30 EC of the major must be level 3. Humanities and Social Sciences methodology requirements are recorded separately because the rules exclude them from the 75-EC BA-major minimum. The remaining 60 EC is preserved as student choice, including the first-year Science breadth course and any further minor, exchange, internship or elective choices, rather than populated with invented subjects. Individual disciplines and tracks remain restricted student choices within the selected interdomain structure.
components: One qualifying course completed no later than semester 4.
For a Fall 2026 entrant: 7.5 EC level-1 Humanities methodology plus at least 7.5 EC level-2 methodology appropriate to the thesis discipline; excluded from the 75-EC BA-major minimum.
7.5 EC level-1 Social Sciences methodology plus at least 7.5 EC level-2 methodology appropriate to the thesis discipline; excluded from the 75-EC BA-major minimum.
Interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences major coursework
Major coursework excluding the separately represented 15-EC thesis; includes tracks in at least two disciplines and at least 15 EC of level-3 track finishers.
Required final-year thesis within the selected interdomain major.
Student choice space, including Science breadth

Student-designed space retained generically; it includes at least one first-year Science course for breadth and may contain further electives, a minor, approved off-campus study, exchange or an internship within the formal limits.

alternatives.label: Society, culture & science
alternatives.concept: A broad Liberal Arts and Sciences programme that connects economics, politics and sociology with philosophy, history and art, alongside life science, ecology, psychology, sustainability and mixed research methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum distributes substantial study across society, culture and science, with economics, politics, sociology, philosophy, history, ecology, health and research methods; the label therefore names all three major domains.
progression: Introductory economics, philosophy, life science, psychology, history, ecology, politics and sociology precede advanced social theory, health psychology, art history and research seminars. The schedule satisfies every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint.

alternatives.label: Society, power & culture
alternatives.concept: A humanities and social-science route organised around power, institutions, culture and inequality, combining history, philosophy, politics, sociology, law, media, literature, art and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum consistently studies society and power through history, philosophy, politics, sociology, law and cultural analysis, so the label captures its central organising fields.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces most economics, natural-science, ecology, health and psychology study with a denser sequence in law, international relations, political thought, history, literature, media and cultural analysis.
progression: Foundations in law, political thought, sociology, history, philosophy, media, art and literature precede international and EU law, international relations, social theory, conflict studies and advanced cultural research. Law, Society & Justice precedes every advanced law course, and all courses meet planned-semester constraints.
traceOverrides: introduces sociological analysis of institutions, identities, inequality and social interaction
compares political institutions and systems using concepts and empirical evidence
examines political, social and cultural transformations in modern history
examines how public communication frames knowledge, responsibility and collective action through the climate crisis

alternatives.label: Life, mind & health
alternatives.concept: A life-science and behavioural route connecting molecular and cellular biology, physiology, disease and laboratory work with neuroscience, cognition, psychology, epidemiology and public health.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains integrated biological, biomedical, neuroscientific, psychological and public-health sequences, so the label accurately identifies life, mind and health as its three connected domains.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with both earlier alternatives, this route replaces most humanities, politics, law, culture and sustainability study with a sequenced laboratory, life-science, biomedical, neuroscience, psychology and health curriculum.
progression: Life-science and brain-and-behaviour foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory work, cognition, advanced biomedical science, psychology and research. Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester and every course is offered in its assigned term.

routeSelection.route: Bachelor of Arts with an interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences major
routeSelection.basis: The generic UCU target does not specify BA/BSc, domain or discipline. The formally available Humanities-and-Social-Sciences interdomain BA major most directly represents UCU's broad interdisciplinary academic identity and the programme overview's cross-disciplinary social and cultural examples. Exact tracks remain student choices; the route was selected before and independently of UCR course selection.

selection.assessment: Two coherent generator-backed directions beyond the broad closest match are feasible and substantively distinct: society, power and culture; and life, mind and health. Both materially change the curriculum and exceed the pairwise 30-EC floor. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached; environment and sustainability, economics and social analysis, and mathematics and physical science remain coherent assessed directions but cannot be added.

blocks: Both develop qualitative social-science research design and analysis; UCU's requirement additionally includes a separate level-1 methods course.
Both require an independently designed research project, but UCU's 15-EC bachelor thesis is larger and sits formally within the major.
The History Research Seminar directly develops advanced humanities research practice, while UCU's component is a broader two-course methodology requirement.
UCU's Academic Core provides a compulsory common foundation; no single UCR course is treated as an equivalent.
The UCU component is a 60-EC restricted interdomain major across at least two disciplines; no individual 7.5-EC UCR course represents that whole structure.
UCU requires a qualifying Language and Culture course; the selected UCR programmes contain cultural study but no equivalent language requirement.
UCU's 60-EC student choice component, including Science breadth, remains open and is not equated to a single UCR course.

notes.text: Both institutions support interdisciplinary Liberal Arts and Sciences, but they organise it differently. UCU requires a formally declared 75-EC BA major, domain-specific methodology, breadth, a Language and Culture course and a 15-EC thesis. UCR uses individually assembled 24-course programmes without formal majors; the three UCR columns therefore show concrete coherent routes rather than reproducing UCU's major architecture.
